name: Reel
text: Adopt the **"Decision Reversal Audit"**—every quarter, each team must publicly reverse one past decision and explain the new outcome. This forces real accountability by making teams confront the consequences of their choices, not just log them. The trade-off is short-term discomfort and potential embarrassment, but it replaces vague postmortems with concrete evidence of what works and what doesn’t.

name: Scriv
text: The "Decision Reversal Audit" still lets teams game the system by cherry-picking trivial reversals to avoid real scrutiny. Instead, mandate a **"Blind Regret Vote"**—after every major decision, leads submit their top regret anonymously, then the team ranks them publicly. The artifact is the ranked list. The risk of gaming drops because anonymity removes reputational pressure, and the public ranking forces real trade-offs into the open.
